scope: Actual-signature authorization boundaries and a real MAC-authenticated witness database composition counterexample; no production protocol/API modification.
observations: A new root changes AccountId despite an unchanged device key/id/generation. Pairing the old account with the new root is refused.
New-root admission and closure of the old root signer do not revoke an independently retained old pin or the original serialized roster. The roster decoder probe is not a full device-journal restart.
The immutable storage owner changes and crossed root/roster scopes refuse. Neither old-root nor new-root issuance can use same-key credential renewal to bridge these roots.
Changing a witness key changes AnchorPin binding even under the same witness instance ID. This is a binding test, not a key-handoff protocol.

In an actual required-witness store, retiring an old device and then enrolling a new-root account still allows trusted-control-plane enrollment of a previously unseen device under the old root. The old device stays retired while both other subjects remain Current after store close/reopen.
interpretation: The existing per-device replacement and pin verification behavior is correct for its documented scope. Composing it with a fresh new-root enrollment does not retire the old root; account-wide durable retirement and independently authenticated application-account continuity need an explicit construction. This is not an unauthorized data-plane enrollment exploit.
limits: Synthetic trusted time 150 and test fixtures, including deterministic signing seeds; not real-time expiry or root-compromise detection.
The witness case performs explicit trusted-control-plane enrollments. Incoming network bytes cannot invoke those operations.

Witness state is exercised through the real local MAC-authenticated witness store and signed replies on macOS arm64 in one process; no process-crash, power-loss, network, foreign-binding, device or platform qualification.
No root-cutover transaction, managed account-trust owner, root-retirement floor or witness-key handoff has been implemented by these probes.
No computational proof or post-compromise secrecy claim follows from finite acceptance/refusal observations.
